item.content:encoded:
I just think it could have a little more on the use of controlling the oxygen content of the chamber. First because you need to guarantee enough oxygen inside despite how much it grows, second because this kind of chamber will be better served by a system to deplete oxygen than water sprinklers, and can have both for greater effect.

Also, it shouldn't cost that much to keep this guy alive. It certainly costs a lot on fuel to keep it at the size needed for interview, but with little fuel it could be kept at candle-flame size, and it seems that it would both solve the problem of fuel and of it being too smart if such size was standard to containment

In reading this article, the thing that makes me ask questions is how much fuel keeping SCP-457 contained uses, and whether the Foundation would be looking for more permanent sources. SCPs like SCP-1689 could work if you consider that potatoes could be dried, and the starch dust used as a fuel source, and if there is one thing 1689 does not seem to have a shortage of, its potatoes. Or, just using SCP-124 to rapidly produce bio-fuel crops. Proposing the following addendum:

Addendum 2: Due to the excessive resource requirements in keeping SCP-457 contained, locating a permanent renewable fuel source is currently a high priority. Proposals so far include, but are not limited to:

  • Use of starch dust obtained from SCP-1689 potatoes.
  • Use of SCP-124 to rapidly produce sources of bio-fuel.

Approval of one or more of these proposals pending review.

Any third SCP suitable for generating fuel could also be included to provide a nice rounded list of three.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!
